comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
🚨 **BLOCKING: `-->` in `withdrawReason`/`fixHunk` corrupts the registry marker — state silently reverts and payload text leaks onto the PR**

The marker protocol embeds the registry payload as JSON inside an HTML comment (`<!-- dmtools:finding-registry {json} -->`). Claims are safe — `normalizeClaim` strips punctuation — but `applyDisposition` stores `disposition.reason` and `disposition.hunk` **raw** (`item.withdrawReason = String(disposition.reason).trim()`), and `buildRegistryComment` serializes them verbatim into the payload. Neither HTML comments nor `extractMarkerJson`'s suffix search can tolerate a `-->` sequence:

1. **On GitHub**, the comment visually terminates at the injected `-->`; the JSON tail leaks into the visible PR thread as garbage text.
2. **On the next round**, `reviewVerdicts.extractMarkerJson` cuts the payload at the **first** ` -->`, `JSON.parse` fails, `registryFromPayload` returns null, the record is skipped — and `latestRegistry` silently falls back to the **previous** round's registry. The reviewer's withdrawal (and everything else registered in the corrupting round) is lost, so the finding stays open and must be re-answered.

Verified repro against this branch (mermaid arrows are pervasive in this repo's comment style, so a reason like `"not a defect: A --> B is handled upstream"` is a realistic trigger):

```
round 2: withdraw F1 with reason "not a defect: A --> B is handled upstream"
buildRegistryComment(...) → "<!-- dmtools:finding-registry {...,\"withdrawReason\":\"not a defect: A --> B is handled upstream\"...} -->"
latestRegistry([that comment], allow) → null          ← round-2 registry unparseable
extractMarkerJson → null (JSON.parse failed)          ← falls back to round 1
```

Suggested fix — sanitize at the boundary where strings enter the payload (either in `applyDisposition` or in `buildRegistryComment` before `JSON.stringify`), e.g. strip or replace marker-hostile sequences from every embedded string field (`withdrawReason`, `fixHunk`, and any future free-text):

```js
function markerSafe(text) {
    return String(text || '').replace(/-->/g, '--\u200b>').replace(/<!--/g, '\u200b');
}
```

(and assert the built body contains exactly one marker suffix, or reject/strip on serialization). The escalation-comment renderer (`buildEscalationPacketComment`) echoes raw reasons too — same treatment there keeps the visible census well-formed.

The unit suite has no round-trip test for marker-hostile payload content — worth adding alongside the fix (`withdrawReason` containing `-->` must still parse back, with the sanitized text preserved for display).

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: comment-list normalization duplicated across the two wiring sites**

`prCommentsForRegistry` (postPRReviewComments.js:1093) and `prCommentListForRegistry` (preparePRForReview.js:243) implement the same "raw comments → array" ladder (`typeof raw === 'string' ? JSON.parse : raw`, then `Array.isArray(obj) ? obj : (obj.comments || obj.items || [])`) with only the error policy differing (catch-and-null vs let-the-caller's-catch-handle). Two independent copies of a parse ladder are exactly the kind of thing that drifts — e.g. if the payload gains another envelope shape, one site gets fixed and the other silently keeps returning `[]`.

Consider hoisting one helper (e.g. `normalizePrCommentList(raw)` in `findingRegistry.js`, or a shared `js/common/` leaf both files already require) and keeping the try/catch policy at each call site. This also conveniently removes three of the twelve over-threshold CRAP functions flagged by the red `crap` gate.

`postFindingRegistryUpdate(ctx, pr, repoInfo, reviewData)` never reads `repoInfo` — the body only uses `ctx`, `pr` and `reviewData`. Either drop the parameter (and update the single call site in `postGitHubReview`) or, if the intent was to reuse the existing `isMachineAuthored({ author: pr.author }, …, repoOwnerOf(repoInfo))` owner carve-out for release-bump PRs, wire it in — as written it just suggests a dependency that isn't there.

comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicate object key — the first `'./common/findingRegistry.js'` entry is dead**

This require map declares the same key twice (lines 188–189 here, and again at lines 2135–2136 in the gh-926 suite):

```js
'./common/findingRegistry.js': loadModule('js/common/findingRegistry.js', makeRequire({ './machineAuthor.js': machineAuthorReal(), './reviewVerdicts.js': … }), {}),
'./common/findingRegistry.js': loadModule('js/common/findingRegistry.js', makeRequire({
    './machineAuthor.js': machineAuthorReal(),
    './reviewVerdicts.js': …
}), {}),
```

In JS the second key silently wins, so behavior is fine — but the first literal is dead weight (looks like a rebase artifact from the require-map fix). Deleting the first entry at both sites keeps the maps readable; no test change needed since both spellings are equivalent.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: Two blockers: the `crap` CI gate is red on head 06e63285 (12 new over-threshold functions in `findingRegistry.js`/`postPRReviewComments.js`), and a verified marker-payload corruption path — a `-->` in a reviewer-supplied `withdrawReason`/`fixHunk` breaks the HTML-comment marker, silently reverting dedup state and leaking JSON onto the PR. The registry design itself (propose/confirm matching, escalate-only merges, fail-closed machine-author gate) is sound, additive, and well tested (7966 passed / 0 failed in CI; the only local failure is a pre-existing env-dependent `sessionDelta` test this PR doesn't touch).

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 **BLOCKING** — Red CI: `crap` ratchet failed, `CRAP may only decrease` (applyRound CC 33, matchFinding 16.1, +10 more; refactor per the gh-1195 split pattern)
- 🚨 **BLOCKING** — `withdrawReason`/`fixHunk` are stored raw and serialized into the `<!-- dmtools:finding-registry … -->` marker; an embedded `-->` makes the next round's parse fail (repro included in the thread) — sanitize marker-hostile sequences at the payload boundary
- 💡 SUGGESTION ×3 — duplicated comment-list normalization across the two wiring sites, unused `repoInfo` param, duplicate object keys in two test require maps

**Next Steps**:
1. Split the over-threshold functions into named helpers (gh-1195 house pattern) and re-run the `crap` gate
2. Sanitize/escape `-->`/`<!--` in every free-text field embedded in the registry marker + add a round-trip test for marker-hostile content
3. Cosmetic: dedupe the comment-list helper, drop the unused param, remove the dead duplicate require-map keys

**Notes**: PR description metrics are stale — `test_findingRegistry.js` holds 57 tests (not 65) and CI ran 7966 (not 7949); the described "identity SHA-256" is implemented as double FNV-1a (fine for per-PR scope, just describe it accurately). Ticket ACs (fingerprinting, propose/confirm dedup, fixed/withdrawn/re-introduced lifecycle, census, fail-closed allowlist, 3-site wiring) are all implemented and covered.
